hypothesis: Most bare losses come from the final guess, not from too little information. 9/10 bare guesses contradict rows the model itself observed (e.g. i105 guessed B=00000000 after seeing B(0,1,1)=1; i128 contradicted 13 observed rows), and i156's guess was 22 bits long. Showing the model the 24 rows in submission order (observed values filled in, '?' for unqueried rows), asking it to decide only the '?' rows, and keeping the observed answers verbatim raises circuit-wise accuracy well above bare's 10% on this batch. Joint correctness stays limited by what the model infers for unqueried rows.
behavior_changes: Final turn: the harness lists all 24 rows in submission order, with the observed answer or '?', and asks the model to list a value for each '?' row and then give a <guess>.

Final guess is assembled by the harness: observed rows use the environment's answers. Each '?' row uses the model's `X(a, b, c) = v` line for that row, or else the matching bit of its 24-bit <guess>. The model gets one follow-up for rows still missing; any row it never answers falls back to 0. Only the assembled <guess> is returned.

A reply with no parseable query, or one repeating an already-answered query, no longer spends the turn: the model is re-asked (at most 6 re-asks per episode). The re-ask for a repeat shows the earlier answer and lists the inputs not yet asked. In bare, i98 lost 3 turns to format failures and asked 4 repeats; i128 asked 1 repeat.
preserved_behaviors: Same system prompt, first user message and per-turn wording ('<answer line>\nPlease send your next query. N queries remaining.').
The model writes every query; the harness never picks one. Same query regex. One env.query per accepted reply.
Same sampling (self.llm defaults); no other model calls added apart from the bounded re-asks and at most one final follow-up.
verification: Ran check_b0r0_cand_labeled6_b10g3r2_b0r0g0.py on all 10 instances: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, queries_used=18 in every episode, 19-21 calls.
OUTCOME: circuit-wise accuracy 18/30 = 60% (bare: 3/30 = 10%). Per instance: 2/3 on 105, 11, 128, 164, 247, 250, 265; 1/3 on 156 and 98; 0/3 on 239. Joint correct still 0/10 (bare 0/10).
Checked res_*.json: 18 unique queries in every episode (bare had 14 in i98 and 17 in i128), so no repeats got through.

Read the i98 final turn: the model's own <guess> turned into a long run of 1s, but its per-row lines were parsed and used, so the guess was valid. Read the i239 final turn: the model kept the observed rows but guessed the 6 unqueried rows wrongly (6/6/6 split, 0/3).

Counted re-asks in the new traces: format re-asks on i128 (1) and i98 (2), no repeat re-asks. Final follow-ups on i164 and i250, and both replies gave every missing row, so the 0 fallback was never used.
risks: Remaining errors come from inferring unqueried rows. The model still sweeps A then B row by row, leaving C 2-4 queries in 7/10 episodes, and its guesses for '?' rows are often wrong. This repair does not touch query allocation or reasoning, so joint accuracy stays at 0 on this batch.
Pushing toward an even split across circuits (a possible next step) could lower circuit-wise accuracy: today's 2/3 scores come from circuits queried on all 8 rows, and i239 (6/6/6 split) scored 0/3.
Unanswered '?' rows default to 0; that is a harness-chosen bit, though it was never needed after the follow-up in this run.
Re-asking after a missing query can loop when the model wants to submit early (i98 bare). The re-asks are capped at 6, after which the loop ends with the remaining budget unspent.
